records: Who was the author of these proverbs?
Solomon, the king of Israel, was the author of these proverbs.
How do these proverbs teach people to live?
These proverbs teach people about what is insightful, righteous, just, and honest.
What can the wise and understanding receive by listening to these proverbs?
Wise people can increase their learning, and understanding people can acquire guidance by listening to these proverbs.
What is the beginning of knowledge?
The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of knowledge.
To whose instruction should a son listen?
A son should listen to instruction from his father and mother.
What should a son do if sinners try to entice him to sin?
A son should refuse to follow those who try to entice him to sin.
With what do those who are sinning plan to fill their houses?
Those who are sinning plan to fill their houses with what they steal from others.
What do those who are sinning hurry to do?
Those who are sinning hurry to do wicked things.
What does unjust gain do to those who gain unjustly?
Unjust gain will kill those who gain unjustly.
Who calls out in the streets, open areas, and city gates?
Wisdom calls out in open areas where busy streets intersect and at the entrance of the city gates.
What did those who lacked wisdom do when Wisdom called out to them?
Those who lacked wisdom ignored what Wisdom said and refused to listen when Wisdom called out to them.
What will Wisdom do when calamity comes on those who lack wisdom?
Wisdom will laugh when calamity comes on those who lack wisdom.
What will Wisdom do when those who lack wisdom call upon her?
Wisdom will not answer when those who lack wisdom call upon her.
With what will those who lack wisdom be filled?
Those who lack wisdom will suffer rightly for their plans and for what they have done.
How will those live who listen to Wisdom?
Those who listen to Wisdom will live safely and not dread evil.
What does the father want his son to store up as precious?
The father wants his son to consider his commandments to be precious.
How should the son seek and search for insight and understanding?
The son should seek insight and understanding as silver, and search for it as a hidden treasure.
If the son seeks and searches for understanding as silver, what will he find?
The son will find the knowledge of God.
What is Yahweh for those who walk in integrity?
Yahweh is a shield for those who walking with integrity.
When wisdom comes into the son’s heart, what will he understand?
The son will understand righteousness, justice, and integrity.
From what will discretion and understanding rescue the son?
Discretion and understanding will rescue the son from the way of evil and from people who speak perversely.
What do those who walk in the ways of darkness forsake?
Those who walk in the ways of darkness forsake the paths of straightness, they refuse to behave righteously.
What does the strange woman forsake and forget?
The strange woman forsakes the companion of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God.
To where do the immoral woman’s tracks lead?
The immoral woman’s tracks lead down to death.
In whose way should the son walk?
The son should walk, or behave like a righteous person.
What will happen to those who live uprightly?
People who live uprightly will stay in this land for a long time.
What will happen to those who are wicked?
Those who are wicked will be removed from the land.
What will the father’s commands and teachings add to his son?
The father’s commands and teachings will add years of life and peace to his son.
Where must covenant faithfulness and trustworthiness be written?
Covenant faithfulness and trustworthiness must be written on the tablet of one’s heart.
On what must the son not lean?
The son must not lean on (rely on) his own understanding.
How must the son not see himself?
The son must not see himself as wise.
What must the son do with his wealth?
The son must honor Yahweh with his wealth.
Yahweh disciplines those whom he loves.
What benefits people more than having silver or gold?
Being wise benefits people more than silver could benefit them. Indeed, being wise is worth more to people than having gold.
What are all the paths of wisdom?
All the paths of wisdom are peace.
What did Yahweh do by being wise?
Yahweh made the world through being wise.
What will be life to the son’s soul?
Prudence and discretion will be life to the son’s soul.
If the son walks in wisdom, what will happen when he lies down?
When he lies down, he will not fear anything, and he will sleep peacefully.
Of what should the son not be afraid?
The son should not be afraid of sudden dread or devastation.
What should the son do for those who deserve it?
The son should not withhold what is good from people who deserve it.
What should the son not do to his neighbor?
The son should not make a plan to harm his neighbor.
Yahweh detests people who act wickedly.
What does Yahweh do to the mockers?
What should the sons not forget?
The sons should not forget their father’s instruction.
How did the father tell the son he would live?
The father told the son he would live by keeping the father’s commands.
What will Wisdom do for the son if the son does not forsake her, but loves her?
Wisdom will watch over him and keep him safe.
What will Wisdom do for the son if the son cherishes and embraces her?
Wisdom will honor him, as if putting a crown of splendor on his head.
In what way did the father teach the son?
The father taught the son in the way of wisdom and directed him in how to live in the right way.
On to what must the son grasp, for it is his life?
The son must consistently remember the things his father has instructed him, for it is his life.
What path must the son avoid?
The son must avoid the path of the wicked ones.
What do the wicked do before they can sleep?
The wicked feel that they must do evil before they can sleep.
What is the path of the righteous like?
The path of the righteous is like the light of the sun that grows brighter until the brightest time of day.
What is the way of the wicked like?
The way of the wicked is like the darkness.
Why must the son guard his heart extremely carefully?
The son must guard his heart extremely carefully, for from it are the sources of life.
What kind of speech and talk must the son put away?
The son must put away speech that deceives or misleads people.
Where must the son focus his gaze?
The son must focus his gaze on doing what is right.
What will the son learn if he listens carefully to what he should understand?
If he listens carefully to what he should understand, the son will learn to be able to choose wisely what to do, and to know the right things to say.
What will happen to you after being with an adulteress woman?
After being with such a woman you will be miserable, as if you had eaten a bitter plant.
To where are such a woman’s feet going?
Her feet are going down to death.
What advice does the father give the sons about getting near any adulterous woman?
The sons are to keep far away from any adulterous woman and not even go near her house.
What will the son give away if he goes to such a woman?
If he goes to such a woman, the son will give away the best efforts of his youth.
What will happen at the end of his life if the son becomes involved with an adulterous woman?
If the son becomes involved with an adulterous woman, he will groan when he is about to die.
What will the son say at the end of his life if he becomes involved with an adulterous woman?
If he becomes involved with an adulterous woman, he will say that he hated correction and despised rebuke.
From where should the sons drink?
The sons should only drink water from their own well, which means to have sex with his wife only.
With what should the a son be exhilarated?
He should be exhilarated by how the wife of his youth loves him.
Whom should the son enjoy sexually?
The father tells the son to enjoy sexually the woman whom he married when he was young.
Yahweh knows everything that people do.
What will capture and grasp the wicked person?
The wicked things that the wicked one does will capture him and his sin will be like cords that grasp him.
How could the son be caught by what he says with his mouth?
The son could regret what he says if he guarantees a loan for a stranger.
What must the son do to save himself?
To save himself the son must humbly go to that person and beg him to cancel what the son has promised.
From what should a lazy person learn?
A lazy person should consider the ant, see its ways, and learn to be wise.
What does the ant do in the summer?
In the summer, the ant gathers and stores food to eat during the winter.
What will happen to the lazy person who does not rise from his sleep?
He will become poor and needy just as surely as if a thief has robbed him.
How would you describe worthless people?
Worthless, sinful people are people who constantly deceive other people by what they say.
What will happen to the wicked man because of his evil plots?
He will be suddenly destroyed and unable to recover.
How many things does Yahweh hate and how many things are abominations to him?
There are six things that Yahweh hates, seven that are abominations to him.
What kind of heart does Yahweh hate?
Yahweh hates the heart of someone planning ways to act sinfully.
What kind of witness does Yahweh hate?
Yahweh hates the witness who lies when testifying.
To what are commandment and law likened?
Commandment is likened to a lamp and the law is likened to a light.
What can having sex with the wife of another cost the son?
Having sex with the wife of another will cause him to die.
Why might people not despise a thief if he steals?
People do not despise someone who steals if he only steals food because he is hungry.
Who does a man who commits adultery destroy?
A man who commits adultery with a woman destroys himself.
What will the one who takes revenge against adultery not accept?
That jealous husband will not accept any money to stop being furious, no matter how much money you offer him.
What must the son keep in order to live?
The son must keep his father’s sayings and commandments to live.
From whom do Wisdom and Understanding keep the son?
Wisdom and Understanding keep the son from immoral women who speak to him seductively.
Who did Solomon notice as he looked out through the window?
Solomon noticed a young man who does not think wisely.
What was the woman wearing who approached the young man?
She was wearing a prostitute’s clothing.
What does the woman do at every corner?
At the corner of any road, she waits for a man whom she can seduce.
What had the woman done that day?
That day, the woman had sacrificed an animal.
For what does the woman look everywhere?
The woman is looking everywhere for the young man.
What does the woman invite the young man to do?
The woman invites the young man to come with her so they can satisfy themselves with lovemaking until the morning.
The woman’s husband is away from home on a long journey.
In what way does the young man follow after the woman?
The young man follows quickly after the woman, going like an ox to its slaughter.
What will the young man’s actions cost him?
The young man’s actions will cause him to die.
What wise instruction is the young man given about an adulterous woman?
He is instructed to not desire her and to never go with her.
What will happen to those who enter her bedroom?
Those who enter her bedroom will die as a result.
Who calls out beside the road?
Wisdom calls out next to the crowded crossroads where everyone can hear her.
What kinds of things does Wisdom speak?
Wisdom speaks of noble things and of what is right.
What is wisdom more valuable than?
Wisdom is more valuable than having precious jewels.
What do those who fear Yahweh hate?
Those who fear Yahweh hate evil, pride, arrogance, and perverted speech.
How do kings and princes who have Wisdom rule?
Kings and princes who have Wisdom rule well.
What is the fruit of Wisdom better than?
The fruit of Wisdom is better than purest gold and the best silver.
What will Wisdom give to those who love her?
Wisdom will give an inheritance to those who love her.
Wisdom was established a very long time ago, before the world existed.
Where was Wisdom when Yahweh made the earth and heavens?
Wisdom was there when Yahweh made the earth and heavens.
What was Wisdom doing beside Yahweh when he made everything?
Wisdom was beside Yahweh helping him to create everything.
Wisdom’s delight was the people he made.
What does one who finds Wisdom also find and obtain?
One who finds Wisdom also finds life and obtains favor from Yahweh.
What happens to the who fails to find Wisdom?
One who fails to find Wisdom hurts himself.
Wisdom has built her own house.
To whom are the invitations that Wisdom sends out directed?
The invitations Wisdom sends out are directed to those who are not wise.
What does Wisdom say to forsake?
Wisdom says to stop acting naively so that you can live well.
What happens to one who rebukes a mocker?
If you rebuke a mocker, that person will hate you.
What happens to one who corrects a wise person?
If you correct a wise person, that person will love you for doing so.
What is the beginning of wisdom?
The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom.
The knowledge of the holy things is understanding.
What are the characteristics of a foolish woman?
A foolish woman speaks loudly, acts naively, but she does not know anything.
Who are in the foolish woman’s house?
Those in the foolish woman’s house are now in the deepest parts of the place where dead people are.
How do fathers react to wise children?
Wise children make their fathers glad.
What does Yahweh do to the desire of the wicked?
Yahweh prevents wicked people from getting what they want.
What becomes of people who are lazy?
People who are lazy become poor.
How does God treat righteous people?
What happens to people who speak foolishly?
People who speak foolishly destroy themselves.
What is found on the lips of a discerning person?
Wisdom is found on the lips of a discerning person.
What happens to people who do not let others correct them?
People who do not let others correct them do what will destroy them.
What happens when there are many words?
People who talk a lot sin a lot.
In what does the blessing of Yahweh result?
It is because Yahweh is blessing them that people become wealthy.
What results when something disastrous happens?
When something disastrous happens, it destroys wicked people.
How do lazy people impact those who send them to do something?
A lazy person is like smoke in the eyes that irritates those who send him.
How long will the years of the wicked ones be?
The years of the wicked ones will be short.
Who does the way of Yahweh protect?
The way of Yahweh protects those with integrity who are honest people.
What does Yahweh do to those who speak perversely?
Yahweh will stop people from speaking who speak perversely.
Presumptuousness or acting proudly comes before disgrace.
What is valuable when Yahweh punishes wicked people?
Righteousness, not wealth, is valuable when Yahweh punishes wicked people.
Desiring bad things will cause people who act treacherously to trap themselves.
What keeps a person away from distress?
A righteous person will be drawn away from distress.
How does the godless person destroy other people?
A godless person destroys others by what they say.
What does a faithful person do instead of gossiping?
A faithful person will keep a matter private instead of gossiping.
What will happen if a person guarantees to pay a debt for someone they do not know?
A person who guarantees to pay a debt for someone they do not know will surely suffer.
What wage does a wicked person make?
The wage of a wicked person is falsehood because they falsely believe that they have gained something good.
Yahweh delights in those who act blamelessly.
Of what can everyone be certain?
It is certain that the wicked will be punished and the righteous will be safely escape punishment.
What happens to the one who generously shares what they have with others?
Those who generously share with others receive even more.
What happens to the one who trusts in his riches?
The one who depends on his riches will not be successful.
What is a tree of life?
The fruit of the righteous, what righteous people say and do, is like a tree with fruit that keeps people alive.
Who will receive what they deserve?
Those who are righteous will be repaid, and much more the wicked and the sinner will get what they deserve.
What does a person who accepts correction love?
A person who accepts correction loves learning what they should know.
Yahweh condemns a person who plans to do what is evil.
A virtuous wife is a husband’s crown.
What kind of directions do the wicked give?
What happens to the families of those who are righteous?
The families of the righteous will continue.
Who is it that cares for their animals?
Righteous people care for their animals.
The sinful things that wicked people say will destroy them.
How does a fool think of what he is doing?
A fool thinks that what he is doing is right.
What are words spoken thoughtlessly like?
Words spoken thoughtlessly are like the thrusts of a sword; they hurt others.
What is in the heart of those who plan evil?
Deceit is in the heart of those who plan evil.
What is an abomination to Yahweh?
Yahweh detests people who speak falsely.
Lazy people will become forced laborers.
Where does the way of the wicked lead them?
The way of the wicked leads them astray; by living wickedly, they destroy themselves.
What becomes of people who do what is righteous?
People who do what is righteous will live.
To what does a wise son listen?
A wise son listens to his father’s instruction.
How does a person keep his life?
A person keeps his life by guarding his mouth.
Who wants things very much and gets very little?
A lazy person wants things very much and gets very little.
What might a rich person have to do in order to stay alive?
A rich person might have to pay out of his riches as a ransom to someone who threatens him.
What happens with people who act proudly?
People who act proudly cause people to argue.
What kind of wealth dwindles away?
Wealth that people gain without working for it will disappear.
What benefits people throughout their lives?
The law of the wise, that which wise people teach, benefits people throughout their lives.
How do prudent people show they are prudent?
The prudent think carefully before they do something.
What will happen to those who let other people rebuke them?
Those who let other people rebuke them for any bad behavior will be honored.
With whom should a person walk in order to become wise?
In order to be wise, a person should associate with wise people.
For whom is a sinner’s wealth stored up?
A sinner’s wealth is stored up for righteous people.
How do parents treat their children if they love them?
Parents who truly love their children are careful to discipline them.
In what condition will the stomach of the wicked be?
The stomach of the wicked will be hungry.
What do the wisest women do?
The wisest women help their families to thrive.
People who behave deceptively show that they despise Yahweh.
What will an honest witness not do?
A witness of who is honest will not lie.
What will happen if you associate with foolish people?
If you associate with foolish people, you will not learn anything from knowledgeable people.
What will happen to the house of the wicked?
The house of the wicked will be destroyed.
What will happen to the tent of the upright?
The tent of the upright will flourish.
What will happen to people who refuse to live righteously?
People who refuse to live righteously will receive from Yahweh what they deserve from living that way.
Does a fool turn away from trouble?
No, a fool confidently interferes in other people’s business.
What does someone do who quickly becomes angry?
A person who quickly becomes angry acts foolishly.
To whom will evil people bow down?
Some day, evil people will bow down in front of good people.
How does Solomon describe those people who plan to do good?
Those who plan to do good are faithful and trustworthy people.
What will people gain if they talk but do not work hard?
If people work hard, they will gain from it, but if people only talk, they will remain poor.
What is a fountain of life?
The fear of Yahweh is a fountain of life which is like a refreshing spring that enables people to live well.
Who shows everyone how foolish they are?
People who quickly become angry show everyone how foolish they are.
Who taunts his maker by his actions?
A person who oppresses poor people is taunting Yahweh, his maker.
What kind of behavior makes a country great?
Acting righteously makes a country great.
What kind of answer calms angry people?
Replying gently to angry people will calm them.
Yahweh watches both the evil and the good.
What is a fool’s attitude toward his father’s correction?
A fool despises the correction of his father.
What kind of sacrifice does Yahweh detest?
The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Yahweh.
What happens to the person who forsakes God’s path?
Yahweh will severely punish the person who refuses to live righteously.
A joyful heart makes the face glad.
What is better than being rich while worrying?
Being poor while reverently fearing Yahweh is better than being rich while worrying.
What kind of person quiets a dispute?
A person who does not easily become angry will help people to be peaceful.
How does a wise son affect his father?
A wise son gladdens his father.
What causes people’s plans to succeed?
When many people advise them well, they will succeed.
Yahweh will tear down what a proud person owns.
What does the righteous person do before answering?
The righteous person thinks carefully before answering.
Where will the person live who behaves better after hearing a rebuke?
The person who behaves better after hearing a rebuke will live among people who are wise.
What teaches a person to be wise?
A reverent fear of Yahweh teaches a person to be wise.
How do all of a person’s ways appear to himself?
All of a person’s ways are pure in his own eyes.
For what has Yahweh made everything?
Yahweh has made everything for its purpose.
By covenant faithfulness and trustworthiness sin is forgiven.
Once a person plans out his way, what does Yahweh do?
A person plans out what he wants to do, but Yahweh determines what he will actually do.
A throne is established by righteousness.
What is a messenger of death?
A king’s anger is a messenger of death.
What should be chosen more than gold and silver?
Wisdom and understanding should be chosen more than gold and silver.
What causes people to ruin themselves?
Being arrogant causes people to ruin themselves.
A person who trusts in Yahweh is happy.
What happens when the wise speak insightfully?
When the wise speak insightfully, what they say causes others to learn.
Even though a way to do things may seem easy and convenient for people, where can it end?
In the end, doing things that way will cause them to die.
People who gossip about others cause friends to stop being friends.
What is the one who signals with his eyes doing?
The one who signals others with his eyes is about to do something perverse.
What is a crown of splendor?
Gray hair is like an honorable crown on the head.
Who is it better to be than one capturing a city?
It is better to be someone who does not become angry quickly than to be powerful and capture a city.
How is the decision of casting lots made?
What does an insightful servant do with regard to a shameful son?
An insightful servant will rule over a shameful son.
To what does an evildoer listen carefully?
An evildoer will listen carefully when people say sinful things that destroy others.
What happens to those who rejoice when someone experiences calamity?
Yahweh will certainly punish people who rejoice when others experience disastrous things.
Why do people who pay bribes think that bribes are magical?
They think that, by paying bribes, everything they do will be successful.
What causes a sensible person to learn?
Rebuking a sensible person once causes him to learn.
What is more dangerous than meeting a mother bear robbed of her cubs?
It can be more dangerous to confront a foolish person who is doing something foolish.
What should a person do before a dispute breaks out?
A person should leave the dispute before it breaks out because once an argument has started, it will be as difficult to stop as it is to stop water that is leaking.
What two types of people are an abomination to Yahweh?
A person who declares a wicked person as righteous and one who declares a righteous person as wicked are both an abomination to Yahweh.
What does a man do who does not think wisely?
A man who does not think wisely agrees to pay someone else’s loan.
What causes a person to experience bad things?
Bad things will happen to a person who thinks and speaks deceitfully.
What helps the body to heal?
A joyful heart helps the body to heal.
What is a foolish son to his father and mother?
A foolish son is a grief to his father and bitterness to his mother.
How can a fool be considered wise?
A fool can be considered wise if he keeps silent.
In what does a foolish person not find delight?
A foolish person hates learning and does not delight in understanding.
How is a wicked person treated?
A wicked person is treated with contempt and a person who acts shamefully, with reproach.
What happens when a foolish person speaks?
What a foolish person says makes people argue and want to beat him.
What deeply affects those who hear it?
What people who gossip say deeply affects those who hear it.
What is a tower of strength?
The name of Yahweh is like a strong tower into which the righteous can run and be safe.
What must a person become before others will honor and respect him?
A person must become humble before others will respect him.
When is it difficult to make someone feel better?
When they are inwardly weak and depressed.
The first person to state his case seems to be right until people whom he knows arrive and question him.
What is more difficult to do than to conquer a fortified city?
It is more difficult to reconcile with an offended relative than it is to conquer a fortified city.
What strongly influences what happens to people?
What people say can influence what happens, even to cause people to die or to remain alive.
How does a rich person answer others?
A rich person answers others harshly.
What must a person have in addition to zeal?
A person must have knowledge in addition to zeal.
What will happen to a person who is a false witness?
Someone will surely punish people who lie easily.
What happens when a poor man calls out to his friends?
When a poor man calls out to his friends, they are gone.
What does a person do who loves his life?
A person who loves his life loves to learn.
What does a person with insight do when offended?
Insightful people do not get angry quickly.
What is like a constant dripping of water?
A quarreling wife is like a constant dripping of water.
From where does a insightful wife come?
An insightful wife is from Yahweh.
How does a person lend to Yahweh?
Giving things to poor people is like loaning them to Yahweh.
Who will have to be rescued a second time?
A very angry person will have to be rescued a second time.
How can a person become wise for the rest of his life?
A person can become wise for the rest of your life by paying attention to what people advise them and by accepting instruction.
What leads people to live for a long time?
Revering Yahweh causes people to live for a long time.
What will a lazy one not do?
A lazy one will not even lift the food to his mouth.
What does a child cause who does violence to his father and causes his mother to flee?
A child who does violence to his father and causes his mother to flee causes shame and embarrassment.
What kind of witness mocks justice?
A worthless witness scorns what is just.
What is the anger of a king compared to?
The king’s anger can frighten people like the roaring of a lion.
What are fools eager to do?
Foolish people are eager to argue with others.
What kind of person is difficult to find?
A faithful person is difficult to find.
What is something that no one can truthfully say about himself?
No one can say truthfully that he has made his heart pure and is clean from sin.
By what is even a young person known?
Even a young man will show others who he is by what he does.
What causes a person to become poor?
If you sleep a lot, you will become poor.
What things are rare and precious?
The knowledgeable things that people say are rare and precious.
What does food gained by deceit taste like afterward?
Food gained by deceiving others tastes like gravel afterward.
What happens to a person who curses his father or mother?
People who curse their parents will be like an oil lamp that is extinguished in a totally dark place.
Instead of trying to pay someone back for a wrong, what should you do?
You should wait for Yahweh to resolve the matter, so that he may vindicate you.
What is it dangerous to thoughtlessly declare?
It is dangerous to thoughtlessly declare that a man will dedicate something to Yahweh before he considers.
Covenant faithfulness and trustworthiness guard a king.
What is the splendor of young men?
The splendor of young men is their strength.
What does Yahweh direct wherever he wants them to go?
Yahweh directs what kings think according to all that he desires.
What is more acceptable to Yahweh than sacrifice?
To do what is right and fair is more acceptable to Yahweh than sacrifice.
What happens to the wealth of someone who acquires riches by a speaking falsely?
That wealth quickly vanishes like mist, and doing that will kill the person who lied.
The wicked are punished because they refuse to do what is right.
What is not seen in the eyes of the wicked?
Grace is not seen in the eyes of the wicked.
Who learns wisdom when a mocker is punished?
The naive learn wisdom when a mocker is punished.
What does a secret gift accomplish?
Where does one who wanders from understanding rest?
One who wanders from understanding rests in the assembly of the spirits of the dead.
Where is it better to live than with a quarrelsome wife?
It is better to live in the wilderness than with an argumentative, nagging wife.
What is a wise man able to bring down?
A wise man is able to bring down the walls that people believe will protect them.
What is the name for a proud and haughty person?
A proud and haughty person is called “Mocker.”
What kind of sacrifice is detestable?
The sacrifice of a wicked person is detestable, and even more so when he offers it while intending to act wickedly.
What things are nothing compared to Yahweh?
Wisdom, understanding, or counsel are nothing compared to Yahweh.
Who gives the victory in the day of battle?
Yahweh determines who wins that fight.
What do the rich and poor have in common?
Yahweh is the maker of both the rich people and poor people.
For what is the reward of riches, honor, and life?
The reward of riches, honor, and life is given to people who are humble and revere Yahweh.
If a child is taught the way he should go, what will he not do when he grows old?
If a child is taught how to behave properly, he will not turn away from that training when he grows old.
What is the relationship between the one who borrows and the one who lends?
The one who borrows is a slave to the one who lends.
What will cease if the mocker is driven away?
Judgment and dishonor will cease if the mocker is driven away.

He said that his friends, as well as he, wanted to be the ones to hear her voice.
What does the young woman want her beloved to do and to be like?
She wants her beloved to hurry and to be like a deer.
What has the city become like even though she was once great among the nations?
The city has become like a widow, alone and without protection.
What can Judah not find even though she lives among the nations?
Judah can find no rest even though she lives among the nations.
Yahweh has afflicted Jerusalem because of her many transgressions.
What has left the daughter of Zion?
All of her majesty and beauty have left the daughter of Zion.
What did Jerusalem remember in the days of her affliction?
Jerusalem remembered all of her precious things that she had in former times.
Because Jerusalem sinned greatly, what is the result?
Jerusalem is now regarded as something abhorrent and defiled.
Who has Jerusalem seen enter her sanctuary even though Yahweh commanded that they must not enter?
Jerusalem has seen the nations enter her sanctuary.
What do the people do as they search for bread?
The people groan as they search for bread.
What has Yahweh spread for the feet of Jerusalem?
Yahweh has spread a net for the feet of Jerusalem.
What is the result of the God placing the yoke of Jerusalem’s transgressions on her neck?
The result is that Jerusalem’s strength has stumbled and they are given into the hands of their enemies.
What has the Lord done to the virgin daughter of Judah?
The Lord has crushed the people of Judah like someone treading on grapes in a winepress.
Why have Jerusalem’s children become desolate?
Jerusalem’s children have become desolate because the enemy has prevailed.
Who has gone into captivity because Jerusalem rebelled against Yahweh’s commands?
Jerusalem’s young women and young men have gone into captivity.
Who died in the city while they sought food to restore their lives?
Jerusalem’s priests and elders died in the city.
What is the result of Jerusalem’s rebellion?
Jerusalem is in anguish and their hearts are completely devastated.
What do the enemies of Jerusalem do when they hear of her calamity?
What does Jerusalem request that Yahweh do to her enemies?
Jerusalem asks that Yahweh would deal with her enemies just as Yahweh has dealt with her for all her transgressions.
How does the Lord express his anger because of Jeremiah’s rebellion?
He has taken away the splendor of Israel and has humbled and brought down the cities of Judah.
How does his anger affect Israel and Zion?
The Lord removed all of Israel’s power, refused to protect them from their enemies, and he allowed them to be destroyed.
How is the Lord’s anger shown?
The Lord has become like an enemy; he destroyed the palaces and the temple and has rejected both the king and priest.
Why does the enemy shout triumphantly?
They shout triumphantly because the Lord abandoned his own holy place and has given the walls of the palace over to them.
What has happened to the gates and bars of Zion?
Her gates have come down, and Yahweh has destroyed and smashed the bars that held them shut.
How do the elders and virgins show they are grieving?
The elders sit on the ground, sprinkle their heads with dust while dressed in sackcloth. The virgins bow their heads down to the ground.
He weeps over the death and destruction of his people and because there is nothing for them to eat or drink.
What do the mockers do as they pass by the city?
They rejoice over the destruction by clapping their hands, hissing and shaking their heads with contempt, and grinding their teeth with hatred.
What does the writer encourage the people of Jerusalem to do?
He says they should cry out to the Lord and lift their hands to him continuously for the sake of their children.
Why are the people begging for Yahweh’s mercy?
They are begging for God’s mercy because they are extremely hungry and because their priests and prophets are being slaughtered.
How does the writer describe the day of Yahweh’s wrath?
On the day of Yahweh’s wrath, the enemy killed young and old, no one survived, and they showed no mercy.
What does the writer say that Yahweh has turned against him all the day?
Yahweh has turned his hand against the writer all day long.
What does the writer say that Yahweh has built around him so that he cannot escape?
Yahweh has built a wall around him and trapped him.
To what animal does the writer compare Yahweh and say that it is waiting to ambush him?
The writer describes Yahweh as a bear that is waiting to ambush him.
What has the writer become to all his people?
The writer has become a laughingstock to all his people.
What can the writer no longer remember since Yahweh has removed peace from his life?
The writer can no longer remember any happiness.
What is the writer’s mood as he calls to mind his affliction?
The writer’s mood is one of deep depression within himself as he calls to mind his affliction.
What does the writer say occurs anew every morning?
The writer says that Yahweh’s merciful actions occur again every morning.
What is Yahweh like toward the one who waits for him and to those who wait in silence for the salvation of Yahweh?
Yahweh is good to those who wait for him and wait quietly for Yahweh’s salvation.
What does Yahweh show, even though he brings grief?
Yahweh shows compassion even though he brings grief.
From where does Yahweh not oppress or torment the sons of men?
Yahweh does not oppress from his heart or enjoy causing grief for the sons of men.
Who is the one who decides what happens—both the bad things and the good things?
The Most High God is the one who decides what will happen.
What should the people do as they search their hearts and examine their ways and turn back to Yahweh?
The people should lift up their hearts and their hands in prayer to God in the heavens.
What should the people admit that they have done against Yahweh as they pray?
They should admit that they have sinned and rebelled against Yahweh.
What does the writer say that Yahweh has made them to be among the peoples?
Yahweh has made them to be garbage and refuse among the peoples.
How does the writer describe the tears that flow from his eyes?
His tears are streams of water that flow out from his eyes.
What does the writer say as his enemies hunt him and silence his life in a pit and cast a stone against him?
He says that he has been cut off and will die.
What did Yahweh tell the writer when he called on Yahweh’s name and asked Yahweh to hear his cry for help?
Yahweh told him not to fear.
What does the writer ask Yahweh to do after seeing his wrong?
He asks Yahweh to judge his case.
What does the writer say he is to his enemies, whether they sit or rise?
He is the object of their mocking song.
What does the writer ask Yahweh to do to his enemies?
He asks Yahweh to pay back to them as much harm as they have done.
What does the writer ask Yahweh to do to his enemies?
He asks Yahweh to pursue his enemies in his anger and destroy them everywhere under the heavens.
To what does the writer compare the people of Jerusalem?
The writer compares the people of Jerusalem to gold that has become tarnished and to holy stones that have been scattered at the corner of every street.
What were the sons of Zion, and how are they now valued?
The sons of Zion were precious, weighed against fine gold, but now they are regarded as clay jars, the work of a potter’s hands.
What does the writer compare the daughter of his people to?
He compares her to the ostriches in the wilderness, who are fierce and do not care for their young.
What happens to the tongue of the nursing baby, and what are the children asking for?
The tongue of the nursing baby sticks to the roof of his mouth with thirst, and the children ask for food, but there is nothing for them.
What has happened to the ones who used to eat the finest food and used to wear scarlet clothing?
The ones who used to eat the finest food are now starving in the streets, and the ones who used to wear scarlet clothing now search through piles of garbage looking for something to eat.
How great is the guilt of the daughter of his people?
The guilt of the daughter of his people is greater than the sin of Sodom.
What were her Nazarites like before, and how are they now?

Her Nazarites were purer than snow, healthy, attractive, and vigorous. Now darkness has darkened their form, they are unrecognizable in the streets, and their skin has shriveled on their bones and become as dry as wood.
What does the writer say about those killed by hunger compared to those killed by the sword?
The writer says that those killed by the sword were better off than those who slowly wasted away from hunger.
What did the compassionate women do with their children?
They boiled their own children and the children became their food.
How did Yahweh bring his wrath to completion?
Yahweh brought his wrath to completion by pouring out his fierce anger and kindling a fire in Zion that consumed her foundations.
What did the kings and the inhabitants of the world not believe could happen to Jerusalem?
They did not believe that an adversary and an enemy could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
What did the prophets and priests do in the city?
The prophets sinned greatly and the priests did evil things, and they poured out the blood of the innocent people right in the city.
What happened to those prophets and priests?
They stumbled about blind in the streets, defiled with blood, so that no one was able to touch their clothes.
What did people shout at the defiled prophets and priests?
People shouted at them to go away, calling them unclean and telling others not to touch them.
Where did the prophets and the priests go?
They fled and wandered among the nations, but the nations said they could not stay.
What did Yahweh do to the scattered prophets and priests?
Yahweh scattered them and will no longer watch over them.
How are the priests received and how are the elders received?
The priests are not respected anymore and the elders are not shown any concern.
What happened when the people watched and waited for help from the nations?
They watched in vain, and the nation they hoped would rescue them was not able to save them.
What did the enemy do to the people?
The enemy tracked their every step so that they could not walk freely through their own streets.
What did the people say about their end?
They said their end was near and the time for their destruction had come.
How does the writer describe the pursuers, and what did they do?
The writer describes the pursuers as swifter than the eagles of heaven; the pursuers set upon them on the mountains and lay in wait for them in the wilderness.
What happened to Yahweh’s anointed, our king?
Yahweh’s anointed was captured in the enemy’s pits.
Why is the daughter of Edom told to rejoice and be glad?
She is told to rejoice and be glad, but the cup of judgment will also pass to her, and Yahweh will punish and humiliate her, too.
What is the daughter of Zion told?
She is told her guilt is ended and Yahweh will no longer keep her in exile.
What is the daughter of Edom told?
The daughter of Edom is told Yahweh will punish her guilt and will uncover her sins.
What does the writer ask Yahweh to do?
The writer asks Yahweh to remember what has happened to them and to see their disgrace.
What does the writer tell Yahweh has happened to their inheritance?
The writer tells Yahweh that their inheritance has been turned over to strangers and their houses to foreigners.
How does the writer describe what is happening to them?
He says that their enemies run after them, that they are weary, and they have reached out to the Egyptians and Assyrians for food.
What are the people saying about their suffering?
They are saying that their fathers sinned and then died, and they are suffering for what their fathers did wrong.
What are the people saying about the slaves?
The people are saying that slaves rule over them and there is no one to rescue them.
How do they describe themselves when they go out to get bread?
They risk their lives to get bread outside the city because violent people in the wilderness will try to kill them.
How do they describe their skin?
Their skin grows hot as an oven from the fever of hunger.
What happened to the women and virgins in Zion and Judah?
Women are raped in Zion and virgins in the cities of Judah.
What happened to the princes and the elders?
Princes are hung by their hands and the elders are shown no honor.
What happened to the young men and boys?
The young men grind with millstones, and the boys stagger under heavy loads of wood.
What happened to the elders and the young men?
The elders ceased from the gate and the young men from their songs.
How do they describe the joy of their heart, their dances, and their honor?
Their joy has ceased, their dances have changed into mourning, and they have lost the honor they once had.
What do they say about their hearts and eyes?
Their hearts have become sick, and their eyes have grown dim because of their tears.
What does the writer say has happened to Mount Zion?
Mount Zion is desolate and foxes roam over it.
What do they say about Yahweh’s reign and throne?
Yahweh reigns forever and his throne is from generation to generation.
They ask Yahweh whether he is forgetting them for so long, and if he will turn them back to himself.
What does the writer fear Yahweh may have done?
He fears Yahweh may have utterly rejected them and may be angry with them beyond measure.
When did Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come to Jerusalem to surround the city and cut off all supplies to it?
Nebuchadnezzar came to Jerusalem in the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah.
Who gave Nebuchadnezzar victory over Jehoiakim king of Judah?
The Lord gave Nebuchadnezzar victory over Jehoiakim.
What did the king tell Ashpenaz to do?
The king told Ashpenaz to bring to Babylon some of the people of Israel, both of the royal family and of the nobility.
What kind of young men did the king want to be brought to Babylon?
The king wanted young men without blemish, attractive in appearance, skillful in all wisdom, filled with knowledge and understanding, qualified to serve in the king’s palace.
What was the king’s daily arrangement for these young men’s food and drink?
Each day the king assigned them a portion of his own food and of the wine he drank, and he arranged for them to be trained for three years.
What were the names of some of these young men from Israel and what names were they given by the chief official?
Daniel was called Belteshazzar; Hananiah was called Shadrach; Mishael was called Meshach, and Azariah was called Abednego.
What did Daniel decide in his heart?
Daniel decided in his heart that he would not defile himself by eating the king’s food or drinking his wine.
What did God cause the chief official to do toward Daniel?
God caused the chief official to show favor and compassion to Daniel.
How did the chief official respond when Daniel asked him to be allowed not to eat the king’s food and wine?

The chief official told Daniel that he feared the king, who had assigned Daniel’s food and drink, and that the king might behead him if he saw Daniel looking worse than the other young men of his age.
What did Daniel ask of the steward who had been assigned over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah?

Daniel asked the steward to test them for ten days by giving them only vegetables to eat and water to drink, and then to compare their appearance with that of the young men who ate the king’s food, and then decide what to do based on what he saw.
After the steward agreed to the test, what did he observe after ten days when he compared Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah to the other young men?
The steward observed that Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah looked healthier and better fed than all the young men who ate the king’s food.
What did the steward do after seeing how well Daniel and his friends looked?
The steward continued to take away their portion of the king’s food and wine and gave them vegetables instead.
What did God give to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah?
God gave them knowledge and skill in all literature and wisdom, and Daniel understood all visions and dreams.
Who brought the young men before King Nebuchadnezzar at the end of the three years?
The chief of the eunuchs brought them before Nebuchadnezzar.
What did the king find when he spoke with the whole group of young men?

The king found that none of them could compare with Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah. In every matter of wisdom and understanding that the king asked them about, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his whole kingdom.
Until when was Daniel in Babylon?
He was there until the first year of King Cyrus.
When did Nebuchadnezzar have dreams that troubled his mind so that he could not sleep?
This occurred in the second year of his reign.
Why did the king summon the magicians, the enchanters, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans?
The king wanted these men to tell him about his dreams.
What did the king tell his advisors about his dream?
The king told them that he had dreamed a dream and that he wanted to know what it meant.
What did the Chaldeans ask the king to do?
The Chaldeans asked the king to tell them the dream so they could tell him what it meant.
What did the king specifically want the wise men to do?
The king wanted the wise men to reveal the dream to him and also to interpret the meaning of the dream for the king.
What did the king say would happen to the wise men if they failed to tell the king his dream and interpret it for him?
The king said that if they failed, their bodies would be cut into pieces and their houses would be turned into piles of rubbish.
What did the king say he would do for the person or people who revealed the dream to him and interpreted it?
The king said he would give that person or persons gifts, a reward, and great honor.
What did the advisors say again to the king?
They said again that the king should tell them the dream, and they would tell him what it meant.
What did the king say the advisors were doing?
The king said that the advisors were trying to get more time because they knew he would carry out what he had said.
What did the king say the advisors had agreed to do?
The king said they had agreed to tell him a false explanation until the situation changed.
Who did the Chaldeans say could do what the king asked concerning his dream?
The Chaldeans said that there was not a man on earth who could meet the king’s demand, only the gods could do that.
How did the king feel after the advisors said they could not tell him his dream?
The king became extremely angry, and he commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be executed.
After the wise men’s reply to Nebuchadnezzar, what did the king decree?
The king decreed that all those known for their wisdom were to be put to death.
How did Daniel interact with Arioch when he came to Daniel?
Daniel replied with prudence and discretion to Arioch. He asked Arioch why the king’s decree was so urgent.
He was the captain of the king’s guard, the one who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
What did Daniel request after speaking with Arioch?
Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time so that he could tell the king what his dream meant.
What did Daniel do when he went to his house?
Daniel told his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah what had happened.
What did Daniel ask his friends to seek from the God of heaven?
Daniel asked them to seek mercy from the God of heaven about the mystery, so that he and his friends would not be killed with the other wise men of Babylon.
What did Daniel do after the secret was revealed to him?
Daniel praised the God of heaven.
What did Daniel say about God’s wisdom and power?
Daniel said that wisdom and power belong to God, and that God’s name should be blessed forever.
What did Daniel say God does with kings and with wisdom?
Daniel said that God removes kings and sets up kings, and that God gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who understand.
What did Daniel say God reveals and knows?
Daniel said God reveals deep and hidden things, and that God knows what is in the darkness because the light is with him.
For what did Daniel thank the God of his ancestors?
Daniel thanked the God of his ancestors for the wisdom and power the God of his ancestors had given him.
Who did Daniel go see after the secret was revealed to him?
Daniel went in to see Arioch.
Daniel told Arioch not to kill the wise men in Babylon. Daniel told Arioch to escort him before the king so Daniel could tell the king the dream’s meaning.
What did Arioch tell the king about Daniel?
Arioch told the king that he had found a man from the captives of Judah who could tell the king the interpretation of his dream.
What did the king ask Daniel?
The king asked Daniel whether he was able to tell him the dream that he had seen and its interpretation.
What did Daniel say about the wise men, enchanters, magicians, and diviners?
Daniel said that they were not able to show the king the mystery that he had asked about.
When Daniel was brought in to the king, who did Daniel say could reveal the mystery the king had demanded?
Daniel said there is a God who lives in the heavens, who reveals secrets.
In general what did Daniel say the king’s dream was about?
Daniel said the dream was about what would happen in the days to come.
What did Daniel say the king had been thinking about while on his bed?
Daniel said the king had been thinking about what will happen in the future, and that God had revealed to him what that will be.
Why was the dream revealed to Daniel?
The dream was revealed to Daniel so that the king might understand the meaning and know the thoughts deep within himself.
What did the statue that the king saw in his dream look like?
The statue was large and had a head of gold, a chest and arms of silver, its middle and thighs were bronze, its legs of iron and its feet part iron and part clay.
What were the feet of the statue made of?
The feet of the statue were made partly of iron and partly of clay.
What happened to the statue the king saw in his dream?
The king saw a stone cut, but not by human hands. The stone struck the statue’s feet and the whole statue shattered into pieces which the wind carried away.
What happened to the stone that struck the statue?
The stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
What did Daniel say he and his friends would do after telling the king his dream?
Daniel said they would tell the king the interpretation of the dream.
What did Daniel say God had given to the king?
Daniel said God had given the king the kingdom, the power, the strength, and the glory.
Who was the head of gold?
King Nebuchadnezzar was the head of gold.
What did Daniel say would happen after the king’s kingdom?
Daniel said another kingdom would arise after his, and then a third kingdom of bronze would rule over all the earth.
What did Daniel say the fourth kingdom would be like?
Daniel said the fourth kingdom would be strong like iron, and it would crush and break all the other kingdoms.
What did the feet and toes made of clay and iron mean?
They meant that the kingdom would be divided, partly strong like iron and partly weak, because the king saw iron mixed with clay.
What did the iron and clay in the toes of the statue represent?
They represented that part of the kingdom would be strong and part of it would be brittle.
What did Daniel say would happen even though the kingdoms would mix themselves by marriage?
Daniel said the kingdoms would not stay united with each other, just as iron does not mix with clay.
What will the God of heaven do in the days of the kingdom that is partly iron and partly clay?
In those days the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed or conquered by another people.
What did Daniel say about the dream and its interpretation?
Daniel said the dream was certain and its interpretation was confirmed.
What did Nebuchadnezzar command to be done for Daniel after he finished telling the king the dream and its interpretation?
The king commanded an offering to be made and incense be offered up to Daniel.
What did Nebuchadnezzar say concerning Daniel’s God?
Nebuchadnezzar said Daniel’s God is the God of gods, the Lord of kings and the one who reveals secrets.
What did the king do for Daniel after the interpretation?
The king made Daniel great, gave him many gifts, and made him ruler over the province of Babylon and chief over all the wise men of Babylon.
What did Nebuchadnezzar do after Daniel made a request of the king?
The king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to be administrators over the province of Babylon.
What were the dimensions of the gold statue that king Nebuchadnezzar made and set up on the Plain of Dura?
The statue was sixty cubits tall and six cubits wide.
Who did King Nebuchadnezzar send to assemble for the dedication of the statue?
He sent messengers to assemble the satraps, the prefects, the governors, the counselors, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates, and all the other officials of the provinces.
Who came to the dedication of the statue that Nebuchadnezzar had made?
The provincial governors, regional governors, and local governors, together with the counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates and all the high officials of the provinces came to the dedication.
What did Nebuchadnezzar want those in attendance at the dedication to do?
He wanted those in attendance to fall down and worship the golden statue when they heard the sound of the horns, flutes, lyres, zithers, harps, and bagpipes, and all kinds of music.
What did the king command to happen to those who did not fall down and worship the statue when they heard all the instruments and the music?
The king said that those who would not fall down and worship, at that very moment, would be thrown into a blazing furnace.
What did the peoples, nations, and languages do when they heard the sound of the music?
They fell down and worshiped the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Who brought accusations against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?
Certain Chaldeans came and brought accusations against them.
What did the Chaldeans say to the king before they accused Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?
They wished the king a long life before making their accusation.
What decree did the Chaldeans remind the king that he had made?
They reminded him that he had decreed that everyone who heard the music must fall down and worship the golden statue.
What did the Chaldeans say would happen to anyone who did not worship the statue?
They said that person would be thrown into a blazing furnace.
Who did not fall down and worship the statue?
Certain Jews, their names being Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, would not fall down and worship the statue.
What did Nebuchadnezzar command when he heard the accusation against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?
He angrily commanded that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought before him, and they were brought before the king.
What did Nebuchadnezzar ask Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?
He asked them if it was true that they did not serve his gods or worship the golden statue he had set up.
What did Nebuchadnezzar tell Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego would happen if they refused to worship the statue?
He told them they would immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace, and no god would be able to rescue them from his power.
What did Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego tell the king?
They told him that they did not need to answer him about this matter.

What was the response of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego to the king when the king repeated the command to fall down and worship the statue, and stated the consequences if they did not follow the king’s command?

Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego responded that their God could and would keep them safe and rescue them from the blazing furnace. But even if not, they would not worship Nebuchadnezzar’s gods or prostrate themselves to the statue.
What did Nebuchadnezzar command concerning Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego?
Nebuchadnezzar ordered the furnace to be heated seven times hotter than normal, and for Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego to be tied up and thrown into the furnace.
How were Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego dressed when they were thrown into the furnace?
They were bound in their cloaks, tunics, turbans, and other garments when they were thrown into the blazing furnace.
What happened to Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego and the men who took them to put them in the furnace?
The men who took up Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were killed by the very hot flames from the furnace and Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego fell into the furnace.
What did Nebuchadnezzar ask his counselors after he saw something amazing in the furnace?
He asked them if they had not thrown three men, bound, into the fire, and they answered that it was true.
What caused Nebuchadnezzar to be amazed and stand up quickly?
Nebuchadnezzar was amazed because he saw four men, not tied up, walking around in the fire and they were not hurt and the brilliance of the fourth man was like a son of the gods.
What did Nebuchadnezzar say to Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego at the door of the furnace?
He called for the servants of the Most High God to come out, and they came out of the fire.
What did those present observe about Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego after they came out of the fire?
Those present observed that the fire had not hurt their bodies; the hair on their heads was not singed; their robes were not harmed; and there was no smell of fire on them.
What did Nebuchadnezzar say about the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?
He said that God was blessed because he sent his angel and rescued his servants, who were willing to give up their bodies rather than serve or worship any other god.
What decree did Nebuchadnezzar issue after the event of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego and the blazing furnace?

Nebuchadnezzar decreed that anyone from any people, nation, or language who spoke against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego would be cut into pieces and their house destroyed, because no other god is able to save like this one.
What did the king do for Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego?
Nebuchadnezzar, the king, promoted Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
To whom did Nebuchadnezzar send the decree?
Nebuchadnezzar sent the decree to all peoples, nations, and languages who lived on the earth.
Why did Nebuchadnezzar send the decree?
Nebuchadnezzar sent the decree to tell everyone about the signs and wonders the Most High had done for him.
What did Nebuchadnezzar say about the Most High?
Nebuchadnezzar said that the Most High’s signs are great and his wonders are mighty, that his kingdom lasts forever, and that he rules over every generation.
How was Nebuchadnezzar living before he had his dream?
Nebuchadnezzar was living securely in his house and prospering in his palace.
A dream that Nebuchadnezzar saw frightened him, and the thoughts and visions in his mind alarmed him.
Why did Nebuchadnezzar issue a decree to bring before him all the wise men of Babylon?
Nebuchadnezzar wanted the wise men of Babylon to come and interpret his dream for him.
What happened when Nebuchadnezzar told his dream to the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners?
They were not able to tell Nebuchadnezzar what the dream meant.
What was Daniel’s Babylonian name and what was Daniel’s position in Nebuchadnezzar’s kingdom?
Daniel’s Babylonian name was Belteshazzar and he held the position of “chief of the magicians.”
Who did Nebuchadnezzar believe was able to tell the interpretation of his dream?
Nebuchadnezzar believed Daniel could interpret his dream for him, for Nebuchadnezzar said of Daniel, “the spirit of the holy gods is in you, so no mystery is too hard for you to explain.”
What did Nebuchadnezzar see in the first part of his dream?
Nebuchadnezzar saw a great, strong, beautiful tree that reached to the heavens. It provided shade for animals and an abode for the birds. It had abundant fruit that fed all living creatures.
What did the holy messenger from the heavens say to do to the tree?
The holy messenger said to chop down the tree, cut off its branches, strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit.
What was to be done with the tree stump?
The stump was to be left in the earth, bound with a band of iron and bronze. Let it be wet with dew. Let it live with the animals. Let his mind be that of an animal and not of a man for seven years.
What was the purpose of doing this to the tree in Nebuchadnezzar’s dream?
The purpose was to show Nebuchadnezzar that those who are alive would know that the Most High rules over the kingdoms of peoples and gives them to anyone he wishes to place over them.
What did Nebuchadnezzar tell Belteshazzar about his other wise men?
Nebuchadnezzar said that none of his other wise men were able to tell him the interpretation of the dream, but Belteshazzar was able because the spirit of the holy gods was in him.
How did Daniel react when he first understood the dream?
Daniel was appalled for a moment, and his thoughts alarmed him.
What details did Daniel repeat about the tree Nebuchadnezzar saw in his dream?
Daniel said the tree had become great and strong, reached to the heavens, and could be seen from all the earth; it had beautiful leaves and much fruit, and animals and birds lived in it.
Who did Daniel say the tree was in Nebuchadnezzar’s dream?
Daniel said the tree was Nebuchadnezzar.
What did Daniel say the holy messenger told Nebuchadnezzar to do to the tree?
Daniel said the holy messenger told Nebuchadnezzar to cut down the tree but leave its stump bound with iron and bronze in the field, wet with dew, until seven times passed over him.
Whose decree did Daniel say was coming upon King Nebuchadnezzar?
Daniel said it was the decree of the Most High that was coming upon King Nebuchadnezzar.
What was to happen to Nebuchadnezzar until he acknowledged that the Most High rules over the kingdoms of people and gives them to anyone he wishes?
Nebuchadnezzar was to be driven from among men. He would live in the fields with the wild animals and eat grass like an ox and be wet with the dew from the heavens.
How long was it to be before Nebuchadnezzar would acknowledge that the Most High rules over the kingdoms of people and he gives them to anyone he wishes?
Seven years were to pass until Nebuchadnezzar acknowledged that the Most High rules over the kingdoms of people and he gives them to anyone he wishes.
What did leaving the stump of the tree represent?
Leaving the stump represented that Nebuchadnezzar’s kingdom would remain for him once he acknowledged that heaven rules.
After interpreting the dream for Nebuchadnezzar, what was Daniel’s advice for him?
Daniel advised Nebuchadnezzar to stop sinning and to do what was right. He also told Nebuchadnezzar to turn away from his sins by showing mercy to the poor.
How long was it before the interpretation of Nebuchadnezzar’s dream began to happen?
All these things began to happen twelve months after his dream.
What did Nebuchadnezzar say about himself as he looked at Babylon?
Nebuchadnezzar said that he had built Babylon by his own power and for the glory of his majesty.
What happened while Nebuchadnezzar was still speaking?
A voice from heaven said that the kingdom had passed from Nebuchadnezzar.
What did the voice from heaven say would happen to Nebuchadnezzar?
The voice said Nebuchadnezzar would be driven away from people to live with the wild animals and eat grass like an ox until he acknowledged that the Most High rules over the kingdoms of people.
What happened to Nebuchadnezzar immediately after the voice spoke?
Nebuchadnezzar was driven away from people, ate grass like oxen, and his hair grew long like eagles’ feathers and his nails like birds’ claws.
What happened to Nebuchadnezzar at the end of the seven years?
Nebuchadnezzar’s sanity was restored to him.
What did Nebuchadnezzar do after his sanity was restored to him?
Nebuchadnezzar praised and honored the Most High who rules forever.
What did Nebuchadnezzar say about the Most High’s power over the earth and the heavens?

Nebuchadnezzar said that the Most High regards all the people of earth as nothing and does as he wishes among the army of heaven and the people of earth, and no one can stop him or question what he does.
The kingdom was given back to him.
What was Nebuchadnezzar’s final statement concerning the King of heaven?
Nebuchadnezzar said, “Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and honor the King of heaven, for all his deeds are right and his ways are just. He is able to humble anyone who is proud.”
For whom did Belshazzar, the king, make a great feast?
He made a great feast for a thousand of his nobles.
He was the grandson of Nebuchadnezzar.
What containers did they use to drink the wine from at this feast?
They used the gold containers that had been taken out of the temple, the house of God, in Jerusalem.
What did the people at the feast do as they drank the wine?
They praised their idols made of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
As the people were drinking wine and praising their idols, what happened?
The fingers of a human hand appeared in front of the lamp stand and wrote on the plaster wall in the king’s palace.
What was the king’s immediate response when he saw the hand?
His face turned pale, his thoughts terrified him, and his legs became so weak that his knees were shaking.
What did the king promise to the one who could explain the writing on the plaster wall and its meaning?

The king promised that the one who explained the writing and its meaning would be clothed in purple and would have a gold chain put around his neck and that he would have the authority of the third highest ruler in the kingdom.
What happened when the king’s wise men came in to look at the writing?
They were not able to read the writing or tell the king what it meant.
What happened to King Belshazzar and his nobles when the wise men could not read the writing?
The king became even more afraid and his face grew pale, and his nobles were confused and did not know what to do.
Who came into the banquet hall because of what the king and his nobles were saying?
The queen came in and told the king not to be afraid and not to let his face turn pale.
According to the queen, what position did King Nebuchadnezzar give to this man?
Nebuchadnezzar made him chief over the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners.
What did the queen tell the king to do?
She told him to call for Daniel, because Daniel would show the king the interpretation of the writing.
According to the king what qualities did he say he had heard about Daniel?
The king said he had heard that the spirit of the gods was in Daniel, and that Daniel had light, understanding, and excellent wisdom.
What did the king tell Daniel about his wise men?
The king said his wise men had been brought in to read the writing, but they were not able to explain its interpretation.
What did the king promise Daniel if he could read the writing and explain it?
The king promised that Daniel would wear purple, have a gold chain around his neck, and rule as the third ruler in the kingdom.
What was Daniel’s response when he was told of the rewards he would receive for reading the writing and explaining its meaning?
Daniel told the king, “Let your gifts be for yourself, and give your rewards to another person. Nevertheless, I will read the writing to you, king, and will tell you the meaning.”
According to Daniel, who gave Nebuchadnezzar the kingdom, greatness, honor, and majesty?
The Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar the kingdom, greatness, honor, and majesty.
What could Nebuchadnezzar do to anyone he wished, according to Daniel?
He could kill or let live anyone he wished, and he could lift up or humble anyone he wished.
Why was Nebuchadnezzar brought down from his kingly throne and why was his majesty taken away from him?
Nebuchadnezzar lost his majesty and his throne because his heart became arrogant and his spirit was hardened so that he acted presumptuously.
Where did Nebuchadnezzar live after he was driven away from people?
He lived among the wild donkeys and ate grass like oxen until he knew that the Most High God rules over human kingdoms.
What were Daniel’s charges against Belshazzar?
Daniel said Belshazzar had not humbled his heart, he had lifted himself up against the Lord of the heavens, and he had not honored the God who held his breath in his hand and who knew all his ways.
According to Daniel, what was sent from God and wrote on the wall?
The palm of a hand was sent from God, and it wrote the message on the wall.
What words were written on the wall?
The words were Mene, Mene, Tekel, and Parsin.
What was the meaning of the writing on the plaster wall?

The meaning was as follows: God has numbered Belshazzar’s kingdom and brought it to an end. Belshazzar is weighed in the scales and found deficient. Belshazzar’s kingdom is divided and is given to the Medes and Persians.
What did Belshazzar do for Daniel after Daniel explained the writing?
Belshazzar had Daniel clothed with purple and a gold chain around his neck, and proclaimed him the third ruler in the kingdom.
What happened that night after Daniel gave his interpretation of the writing to Belshazzar?
That night Belshazzar, the king of the Chaldeans, was killed, and Darius the Mede received the kingdom.
How old was Darius the Mede when he received the kingdom?
Darius the Mede was sixty-two years old when he received the kingdom.
Who did Darius appoint over the kingdom?
He appointed 120 satraps, with three sareks over them.
Who was one of the three sareks?
Daniel was one of the three sareks.
Why were the three sareks appointed?
They were appointed to supervise the satraps, so that the king would not suffer any loss.
Who was the king planning to put over the whole kingdom?
The king planned to put Daniel over the whole kingdom.
Why could the other sareks and satraps find no corruption, mistakes, or negligence in Daniel’s work for the kingdom?
They could find nothing against him because Daniel was reliable and trustworthy.
What was the only area where the other sareks and satraps thought they might find something to accuse Daniel of?
They thought they might find something against Daniel regarding the law of his God.
Who went together to speak with King Darius?
The sareks and satraps went together to speak with King Darius.
What did the satraps and the other sareks advise King Darius to do?
They advised Darius to issue a decree that whoever made a petition to any god or man except King Darius for thirty days would be thrown into a den of lions.
What did the sareks and satraps ask King Darius to do?
They asked him to set up the decree and sign it, so that no one could change it, according to the law of the Medes and Persians.
What did King Darius do with the decree?
What did Daniel do after he learned that the decree had been issued and the document signed into law?
Daniel went into his house, got down on his knees and prayed, giving thanks to God as he had done many times before.
What did the men find Daniel doing?
They found Daniel praying and asking for help from his God.
What did the king say when the men asked him about the decree?
The king said that the decree was certain, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be changed.
What did the men who plotted against Daniel do when they saw Daniel make requests and seek help from God?
Those men went to the king and told him that Daniel paid no attention to the king or his decree and that Daniel prayed to God three times a day.
What did the king do when he heard Daniel had disobeyed the king’s decree?
The king became very distressed, and he tried hard to find a way to save Daniel.
What did the men remind the king about the law of the Medes and Persians?
They reminded him that any decree or law the king makes cannot be changed.
What did the king say to Daniel before he was thrown into the den of lions?
The king said, ‘May your God, whom you serve continually, deliver you.’
After Daniel was thrown into the lion’s den, what did the king do?
The king sealed the entrance to the den with his own signet ring. He then went to the palace and fasted through the night and did not sleep.
What did the king do at dawn?
The king got up at dawn and went quickly to the den of lions.
The next day after Daniel was thrown into the lions den, when the king went to the den, what did he ask Daniel?
The king asked Daniel if the God whom Daniel served continually had been able to save him from the lions.
How did Daniel answer the king?

Daniel said to the king, “King, live forever! My God sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not harmed me, because I was found innocent before him, and I have also done no wrong to you, O king.”
What did the king command after he saw that Daniel was alive?
The king rejoiced and commanded his servants to bring Daniel up out of the den.
What did the king command be done to the men who had accused Daniel?
The king commanded that the men who had accused Daniel, along with their wives and children, be thrown into the den of lions.
Who did King Darius write to?
He wrote to all the peoples, nations, and languages living in all the earth.
What did Darius say concerning God in his decree about the God of Daniel?

Darius said that the God of Daniel is the living God who will endure forever and whose kingdom will never be destroyed. God rescues and saves people and does signs and wonders in heaven and on earth; he rescued Daniel from the lions.
During whose reign did Daniel prosper?
Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and during the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
When did Daniel have a dream and visions in his mind?
Daniel had a dream and visions while lying on his bed during the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon.
In Daniel’s vision, what was stirring up the Great Sea?
The four winds of the heavens were stirring up the Great Sea.
What came up out of the sea?
Four large beasts, each different from the others, came up out of the sea.
What was given to the beast that was like a lion?
The mind of a man was given to it.
What was the bear-like beast told to do?
It was told to get up and eat as much meat as it wanted.
What was the leopard-like beast given?
It was given authority to rule.
What did the fourth beast do?
The fourth beast devoured, crushed, and trampled what was left with its feet.
What did Daniel see happen to the fourth beast as he considered its horns?

Daniel saw another little horn grow up among the other ten horns. Three of the first horns were torn out. Daniel saw that the little horn had eyes like a man and a mouth that boasted about great things.
Who sat on one of the thrones that was set up?
The Ancient of Days sat upon one of the thrones.
What business was being conducted by the Ancient of Days?
The court was in session and the books were opened.
What happened to the four beasts?

The beast with the horn that spoke boastful words was killed, its body destroyed, and it was given over to be burned up. The other three beasts had their authority to rule taken away, but their lives were allowed to continue for a time.
In Daniel’s vision, who was presented to the Ancient of Days?
One who came with the clouds of heaven like a son of man was presented to the Ancient of Days.
What was given to this one who was “like a son of man”?
Everlasting authority to rule, glory, and a kingdom that will never be destroyed were given to this one who was “like a son of man.”
How did Daniel feel because of his vision?
Daniel felt very troubled and alarmed because of what he saw.
What did Daniel do to understand his vision?
Daniel went to one of those standing there and asked him what it all meant, and that one explained the interpretation to him.
What was Daniel told the four beasts represented in his vision?
Daniel was told that the four beasts were four kings that would arise from the earth.
Who will receive the kingdom and possess it forever?
